body.name: Pulled-coordinate coupled scalar--harmonic nested derivative
body.construction:
Put \(e=e_{C1}-e_{C0}\).  For the inner problem, solve the scalar pushforward equation on the selected branch at a fixed harmonic coordinate \(a\), and denote its reduced intrinsic quadratic cost by \(\mathcal J_p(a)\).  At \(a=a_p\), transport optimality gives \(\nabla_a\mathcal J_p(a_p)=0\).  Let \(b_p=\dot a_p\) be determined by the differentiated finite-dimensional equation
\[
 \nabla_a^2\mathcal J_p(a_p)b_p
 +D_{(f_{C0},f_{C1})}\nabla_a\mathcal J_p(a_p)
       [\delta_{C0},\delta_{C1}]=0,
\]
and let the mean-zero pulled-back scalar increment \(u_p\) solve
\[
 \mathcal L_{\mathsf C}u_p
 =\Pi_0\!\left[e+\operatorname{div}(\mathsf C b_p)\right].
\]
Thus the complete pulled-back inner differential is \(b_p+\nabla u_p\).  The pulled-back generated-target tangent entering the outer equation is
\[
 r_T=\alpha e+e_{T0}-e_{T1}
 -(\mathsf C\nabla\alpha)\mathbin{\cdot}(b_p+\nabla u_p).
\]
For the outer problem, solve its scalar pushforward equation at fixed harmonic coordinate and denote the reduced cost by \(\mathcal J_T(a)\).  Let \(b_T=\dot a_T\) be determined by the differentiated equation
\[
 \nabla_a^2\mathcal J_T(a_T)b_T
 +D_{(f_{T1},q)}\nabla_a\mathcal J_T(a_T)
       [\delta_{T1},\dot q]=0,
\]
where
\[
 \dot q=p\#\delta_{T0}
 -\operatorname{div}\!\left(q\,(b_p+\nabla u_p)\circ p^{-1}\right),
\]
with the inner field interpreted before the pullback.  Let the mean-zero outer scalar increment \(u_T\) solve
\[
 \mathcal L_Bu_T=\Pi_0\!\left[r_T+\operatorname{div}(B b_T)\right].
\]
Define
\[
 \mathcal D_P[\delta]=(b_T+\nabla u_T)_{\mathcal Y_J}.
\]
Equivalently,
\[
 \mathcal D_P[\delta]=\mathcal H_P[\delta]
 +\left(
 \nabla\mathcal L_B^{-1}\Pi_0[\alpha e+e_{T0}-e_{T1}]
 -\nabla\mathcal L_B^{-1}\Pi_0[(\mathsf C\nabla\alpha)\mathbin{\cdot}
       \nabla\mathcal L_{\mathsf C}^{-1}\Pi_0 e]
 \right)_{\mathcal Y_J},
\]
where the full harmonic correction is
\[
 \mathcal H_P[\delta]=\left(
 b_T+\nabla\mathcal L_B^{-1}\Pi_0\!\left[
 \operatorname{div}(B b_T)
 -(\mathsf C\nabla\alpha)\mathbin{\cdot}b_p
 -(\mathsf C\nabla\alpha)\mathbin{\cdot}
 \nabla\mathcal L_{\mathsf C}^{-1}\Pi_0
       \operatorname{div}(\mathsf C b_p)
 \right]\right)_{\mathcal Y_J}.
\]
